topics.title: Server update notices
topics.body:
Carribrary checks official GitHub releases when an administrator opens the dashboard. The server contacts GitHub at most once a day; no library records, borrower details or service keys are sent. GitHub receives the server internet address and a generic Carribrary update-check identifier. Preview installations can see newer previews and stable releases. Stable installations show only stable releases.

1. Look for a new-version notice above the dashboard.
2. Create and verify a complete backup. Keep a copy on another device.
3. Select Release notes and server downloads. Choose the Windows EXE, Linux x86_64 Flatpak or Raspberry Pi ARM64 DEB for your server.
4. Follow the existing Update the server instructions. The notice does not install anything automatically.

Dismiss this version hides that notice on this browser only. A newer version can still appear. To check again, open Server updates at the bottom of the administrator page and select Check for updates. Checks are shared across administrators and limited to once a minute even when requested manually. If GitHub is unreachable, your library keeps working. A previously discovered update may still be shown with a warning. Server update notices are for administrators, not borrowers. The iPhone librarian PWA also shows them; install the update on the server computer.

topics.title: Borrower dashboard and navigation
topics.body:
Your Catalog still opens first after sign-in. It now uses the same layout, colors, library icon and sidebar artwork as the librarian dashboard, with borrower-only navigation.

1. Review My loans & due dates and My holds & requests above the catalog. These show only your own borrowing activity.
2. On a phone or narrow tablet, tap Open navigation to see Catalog, My reading, My loans and Account. Tap Close, tap outside the sidebar, or press Escape to close it.
3. Search the catalog, filter by Collection, sort and choose 10, 25 or 50 books per page as before. The top search bar on larger screens also searches Catalog.
4. Use Self-checkout or Self-return only if your librarian has enabled them for your account. These actions appear beneath the overview.

A request holds a copy while awaiting approval; a hold is not a loan until the book is handed over. Reporting a return leaves the book on loan until the librarian confirms physical receipt. My reading and Account retain your encrypted private lists, device settings and account deletion safeguards. This layout does not grant librarian access or change borrowing permissions.

The shared catalog uses the same branded sidebar too. Visitors who have not signed in see only Catalog and Sign in / account in that sidebar. Browsing, requesting and suggesting books remain available without an account; no administrator or private-account controls are exposed.

topics.title: Mobile borrower artwork
topics.body:
Library branding is shared across borrower catalog, sign-in and account pages. Existing artwork does not need uploading again.

1. Open Settings & Tools → Library & Appearance → Theme & artwork. Select your saved theme, or choose New theme.
2. Under Mobile borrower artwork, choose a PNG if you want a separate phone image. Recommended size: 512 pixels wide × 1024 pixels high. Maximum original: 10 MiB and 8192 pixels per side. Carribrary fits it without cropping; saved limit: 2 MiB. Use main artwork on phones removes the optional image.
3. Under Borrower header composition, choose Portrait or Landscape. Each has its own compact control group beside a live preview. On narrow screens the preview sits above the controls and stays visible while you scroll through them. Percentages appear beside their labels. Switching orientation keeps your unsaved adjustments. Full image shows the whole picture with library-colored space around it. Fill header fills the area but may crop edges. Horizontal focus moves left/right; Vertical focus moves up/down. These settings stay separate when a device rotates.
4. Adjust Readability overlay to keep words and buttons clear. Check the live preview, then switch orientation to check the other view. Text wraps naturally; previews inside a narrow editor may be narrower than the device shown.
5. Give the theme a name and select Save & use theme. Refresh open borrower pages once to load the saved settings. Rotation and resizing then work without refreshing.

900 pixels is the screen-width breakpoint for the navigation drawer, not an image size. The mobile image is used in borrower headers up to 1200 screen pixels wide, including landscape tablets; the drawer uses it up to 900 pixels. Wider pages use main artwork. Headers never stretch images. In Full image mode all source pixels remain visible, though text still overlays the decoration. Use artwork without small printed text for best results.

Saved themes remember colors, both images, portrait/landscape fitting, focus and overlay. New theme and built-in presets clear artwork and reset header controls. Existing uploads default to Full image. Backups include these settings. Images are public branding, never private records. Android librarian artwork remains the main library image. Avoid downgrading after configuring new branding settings.

Server readability: in the same Theme & artwork editor, use Server artwork readability. Sidebar readability darkens the main sidebar artwork; Header readability adds the library page color behind the server header and Dashboard heading. Adjust both in the live server preview, then Save & use theme. These values are saved with the named theme, included in backups, and separate from borrower portrait/landscape controls. Higher percentages mean a stronger layer. Presets and New theme use default values; older uploads remain supported.

topics.title: Library icon: sizes, transparency and upload errors
topics.body:
1. Open Settings & Tools → Library & Appearance → Library identity.
2. Choose a PNG, JPEG or WebP. A square 512 × 512 transparent PNG is recommended. Larger sources are allowed: at most 10 MiB and 8192 pixels on either side in the browser. Android also limits decoded images to 20 million pixels.
3. Wait for Ready to save and review the preview. Carribrary makes 192 × 192 and 512 × 512 PNGs without cropping. Transparent padding stays transparent. Each saved image may be up to 2 MiB. Detailed designs are allowed; visual complexity itself is not blocked.
4. Select Save library identity. Refresh open library pages. Home-screen shortcuts may need removing and adding again to refresh an old icon. The native Android launcher icon remains Carribrary.

If upload fails, read the size or format message. A broken image cannot be saved as a replacement. Choose another file or Use Carribrary icon before saving. An error does not remove the previously saved icon. Avoid tiny text and fine details that will be hard to see at phone-icon size.

topics.title: Unsaved changes, saving and Cancel
topics.body:
On the server dashboard, iPhone/browser companion and borrower reading pages, when you edit a browser form, changes stay in that open form until you save.

1. Fill in the fields, then choose the action button, such as Save library identity or Save my reading.
2. While the action is running, keep the page open. The status explains that work is in progress; some navigation and Cancel controls are temporarily unavailable.
3. If an error appears, your entered information stays in the form. Read the message, correct the problem and try again. If a connection was lost, refresh the current library state before repeating a checkout or other operation.
4. Cancel, Back or leaving an edited form can ask whether to discard unsaved changes. Choose Cancel in that browser prompt to keep editing, or OK to discard. Closing/reloading the browser may use the browser's own wording.

Help with this page opens relevant instructions in a separate tab so your draft stays open. Read-only Help searches do not count as library edits. Draft protection keeps data in memory only; it is not an automatic draft backup. Saved borrower private reading is still encrypted by the existing private-list system.

topics.title: Windows setup progress and a stalled installation
topics.body:
The Windows installer shows its stages in the details pane and a small progress window. Preparation checks ports, stops an existing service and creates a recovery copy when applicable. Configuration verifies program files, preserves settings, prepares HTTPS, imports an optional backup, registers the service/firewall and checks startup.

1. Keep setup open and read the current stage. A large recovery copy can take several minutes. The elapsed display updates between stages and while external helper commands run; it is not an estimate of time remaining.
2. If setup reports an error, keep the message and the setup log path. A failing external HTTPS preparation helper is limited to three minutes; an optional import helper to fifteen minutes. Recovery snapshot copying is not force-killed by those helper limits.
3. Logs are in C:\ProgramData\HomeLibraryNative\setup-logs. Keep them private. Carribrary retains the ten newest setup logs. Helper details and diagnostic reports can include additional local paths.
4. If the same stage appears stuck, do not start another installer or delete library data. Note your Windows version, installer version and stage. Contact support with a short redacted excerpt or screenshot. Avoid sending full logs/backups unless support asks for a safe excerpt.

Setup progress improvements help diagnose a stall; they do not establish the cause of any unconfirmed installation report. Existing program recovery and complete-backup recovery remain separate.

topics.title: Libraries & network: choose the right setup
topics.body:
Open Settings & Tools → System & Advanced → Libraries & network on the server computer. Sign in as a local administrator first. A paired phone cannot change the computer’s hosting setup.

Choose New library on this computer for separate books, readers, administrator sign-ins, phone pairings, appearance and backups on one computer. Choose Library on another computer when each library has its own computer. If you only need separate shelves with shared readers and loans, use Collections instead.

No live router settings change automatically. Review the port table and enter the rules in your router’s app or website. Keep every server awake while people use it.

topics.title: Create another library on this computer
topics.body:
1. Open Libraries & network. Choose New library on this computer.
2. Enter its name and choose Create separate library. Carribrary chooses unused ports and a separate data folder. Your first library keeps its books.
3. On Windows, open the Windows hosting assistant, review its list, approve the administrator prompt and apply setup. This prepares each library’s private HTTPS key.
4. Choose First sign-in steps for the new library. Keep the setup code private. Open that library, paste its code and choose its own administrator name and password.
5. Add its books and configure its own sharing and Devices page.

Pause stops only that additional library; Start resumes it without deleting its data. Extra libraries run while the main server runs. Back up every library separately from its own dashboard. The main complete backup does not include other libraries’ data. If an additional library’s data is missing after recovery, restore its own backup; Carribrary will not create an empty replacement automatically.

Complete Backup Recovery from the application menu targets the MAIN installation. Do not restore an extra library’s archive over the main library. Moving an extra library to its own replacement computer is supported: install a fresh server there and rehearse/restore that extra library’s portable complete archive. Recovery into an additional-library slot on this same computer currently needs assisted recovery; contact support first. The additional dashboard explains this instead of opening the main recovery shortcut. If the server is not responding, the recovery guidance still explains these main-versus-additional limits without launching a recovery operation.

topics.title: Share two libraries through one home internet connection
topics.body:
Each public library needs a different hostname, such as familybooks.duckdns.org and churchbooks.duckdns.org. Both hostnames point to the same public IP. Create them at https://www.duckdns.org/ . Keep the first computer as the public entry.

1. On the first computer, finish Public sharing setup and verify it works from a phone with Wi-Fi OFF.
2. For another library on this same computer, choose its Public hostname in Libraries & network. Enter its different hostname. Optionally save the DuckDNS token from the account that owns that hostname. Save. Only that additional library restarts.
3. For a library on another computer, follow Prepare the second computer and Connect it on the first computer below.
4. Keep router TCP 80 and 443 pointed at the FIRST computer only. Windows uses destination ports 80/443; Flatpak and Pi use 8080/8443. Carribrary routes each hostname to the right library. Do not forward the loopback dashboard, internal catalog or discovery port.
5. Open both HTTPS hostnames with phone Wi-Fi OFF. Each must show its own library. Create sharing links and pair phones from each library’s own dashboard.

Native Android remote connections keep their separate secure phone ports. Use the exact table in Libraries & network. Each outside phone port must be different. Browsers and PWAs only need the first computer’s 80/443 rules.

topics.title: Prepare and connect a library on another computer
topics.body:
On the SECOND computer:
1. Install Carribrary, complete first administrator sign-in and keep both computers on the same home network.
2. Reserve its local IP address in your router. Open Libraries & network → Library on another computer → I’m on the second computer.
3. Enter this library’s different public hostname, choose its listed home-network address and keep the suggested private connection port unless it is used. Optionally enter the DuckDNS token for THIS hostname. Choose a different outside Android phone port, usually 7444 for a second server.
4. Review the checkbox and save. This replaces this computer’s managed browser proxy with a private encrypted connection through the first computer. Existing phone pairings stay valid. Restart Carribrary. On Windows use its hosting assistant to prepare keys, allow the private bridge and restart.
5. If a local firewall is active, use its graphical firewall tool to allow the displayed private TCP port from your home network. Never forward this private bridge port on the internet router.
6. Download the private connection file. Carry it privately, for example on a USB drive, to the first computer. It is a credential, NOT the borrower QR. Never post it or attach it to a support report.

On the FIRST computer:
7. Open Libraries & network → Library on another computer → I’m on the first computer. Select the private file. Check the displayed library name, hostname and address. Choose Verify and connect. Carribrary checks the certificate and library identity before adding the route.
8. Test both public HTTPS names using mobile data. Delete spare copies of the private connection file after setup. If verification fails, check that the second computer is on, restarted and permits its private port. No unverified route is added.

Pause public route stops forwarding to that computer. Disable private connection on the second computer rejects its bridge credential immediately. To reconnect after disabling, export a new private file and set up the connection again. Each computer keeps its own books and backups.

topics.title: Windows hosting assistant: review and undo
topics.body:
Use Start → Carribrary → Libraries and network, or Open Windows hosting assistant inside the local hosting page. Windows asks for administrator approval.

1. Read the listed libraries, phone ports and public hostname. Finish any edits before continuing.
2. Check I reviewed these changes. Choose Apply reviewed setup.
3. The service briefly stops. The assistant prepares machine-bound HTTPS keys and adds only Carribrary’s named firewall rules. It restarts the service when finished.
4. Reopen Carribrary and check each library. Test public access using a phone with Wi-Fi OFF.

If this installation already used Carribrary’s older scheduled public proxy, the assistant pauses that task and keeps its configuration. Undo public-proxy migration restores its previous enabled/running state and stops the new managed public routes. It keeps library data and keys. Other custom reverse proxies are not rewritten. On a replacement Windows computer, run the assistant again; copied readiness files are not treated as permission to reuse another computer’s machine keys or firewall setup.

topics.title: Household reader: install your personal reading app
topics.body:
This is for a household reader with a personal reading link, including a librarian’s own reader profile. Borrower accounts still install through Account → This device. The optional paid Android app is for librarians, not household reading.

1. Ask the librarian to open Reading tracker, select your household reader and create a personal reading link. Public HTTPS must be set up first. Open that private link on your phone.
2. Open This device · install reader app. Choose Install reader app. In Chrome accept Install when offered. On iPhone use Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen → Open as Web App, if shown → Add.
3. Open the new library icon. If it asks for your personal link, paste the full link from your invitation. The link is deliberately not put in the public installation manifest.
4. On YOUR OWN device only, optionally select Remember my private reading link on this device. Anyone using this browser profile or installed app can then open it. Use a device lock. On a shared device leave this off.
5. To remove the remembered link, open This device and choose Forget saved reading link. Keep your original invitation to return later. Ask the librarian to replace the link if someone else has it.

The reader app has a separate app identity from the borrower and librarian apps. It does not grant administrator access. Private books and notes are not cached offline; keep a connection to your library. Some iPhones keep browser and installed-app storage separate, so you may need to paste the link once inside the installed app. A local HTTP address with a certificate warning cannot provide normal secure PWA installation.
